pr_title: Fix WLED power and brightness with WLED 0.10+
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

WLED 0.10 introduced the possibility to control individual segments of a single LED strip and gave those individual power and brightness states/controls.

This was implemented in #36091, however, it didn't work out as documented/expected. Resulting in a current broken state of the integration when using the current stable version of WLED: 0.10

### The problem

WLED has brightness & power controls on device level AND on an individual segment level. Basically, they are not related. If one controls the master levels, the segment levels won't reflect that change. e.g., turning off a device, does not turn off the segments. Turning on a segment, does not turn on the device.

Brightness is similar, except the final brightness is calculated based on both the master & individual segment brightness.

I've checked with the author of WLED to see what is going on, as this isn't documented, so it might have been a bug. As it turns out, it isn't a bug.

### Current state

The current state of the component does not take that into account. Hence, the on/off light state is incorrect / not working, and brightness works partially right now.

### The Fix

This PR implements a fix for this, to be both userfriendly when having just 1 segment (whole strip), but having full control when implementing multiple segments. In such a way it fixes the current issues.


If 1 segment is defined (single control the whole LED strip):

- 1 Light entity is created. It takes the master controls into account, making is just a simple light in Home Assistant.

When 2 or more segments are defined:

- A master control light is created additionally. The additional light gives control over the master power and brightness. 
- Other light entities will no longer control master to stay close to WLED functionality.

### Additionally

This PR bump `wled` to v0.4.2. Changelog <https://github.com/frenck/python-wled/releases/tag/v0.4.2>.

Existing tests are adjusted and new ones provided to keep a 100% coverage on the full integration.

Documentation has a PR open as well, to document this behavior.

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->

When using WLED 0.10, the brightness value and the on/off state of a LED segment is incorrectly displayed in Home Assistant.

In these cases, the state brightness and on/off state of the strip as a whole is shown instead of the individual segments.

Changing states, does control the individual segment, after the data coordinator pulled in the current state, it is incorrectly displayed again.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.111.0b0
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): new feature
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): Any
- Integration causing this issue: WLED
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integration/wled

comments:
This actually is pretty nasty, as there are now 2 different states. One for the strip as a whole and one for the segments. Home Assistant shows the segments as a light.

Maybe an additional switch needs to be added in order to be able to control the LED strip as a whole. In the current form, controlling WLED with 0.10 firmware is pretty useless 😢

Just thinking out loud but maybe a [light group](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/light.group/) would be a better fit for the light strip as a whole because the segments are a group of lights from the entire light strip.  Also by default isnt there just 1 segment until the user creates them or are there none? Personally I don't use segments.
Integrations like Hue will also expose groups of lights as entities. I think that is similar to WLED segments (indivudual lights) in a strip (a group).

It becomes a bit weirder after more serious testing those new features. The on/off state of a segment does not reflect the actual state.

Clarification: Turn off the main power state, does not change the segment states (those will keep their original power state value).

Furthermore, the segment power state does not override the main power state. So if the main power state is off, and the segment is turned on, the strip (including the segment) will remain off as well.

Furthermore, the brightness is defined at device level and segment level as well. The master device level brightness seems to have a multiplier effect on the brightness set to each individual segment.

So if you use the master brightness setting, you see the segments equally dim/brighten in relation to their individual brightness settings.

In conclusion, I think the only way to fix this is by:

- Add a master light entity, with on/off & brightness control
- Add a light entity for each segment.

This can be confusing if one doesn't use segments. However, the UI from WLED has that exact same confusion. Optionally, I could withhold exposure of a master light in HA when segments are not used, but even if that is the case the UI of WLED still offers those features and one can end up in a weird out of sync state.

Additionally: This all only applies to WLED 0.10 and newer. Before that, segments didn't have brightness or power state control.

I've dropped the question @ WLED on if this is intended working or an issue in the new features. Hopefully, I get a response soon.

Oh man, that's a lot of options. I can see how they got there, I can also see how that is going to be confusing.

Could we make an exception when there is only 1 segment and just have a single entity ?

Talked to the author of WLED. It is indeed intended functionality, unfortunately, undocumented in both user and API documentation.

The WLED app and web interface will still have those master controls, even with 1 segment.

I could "force" the segment power & brightness state to match the master state with 1 segment, but that still feels like breaking the actual WLED functionality + displaying current state becomes a problem (which one to pick if the brightness of the master and segment are not the same?!)

It becomes more complicated when having backward compatibility.

Going to sleep over it and play tomorrow.

Ah yes, I forgot the WLED app. We can't just take our own approach or we would break the WLED app. 

In a perfect world with 1 segment and no other app to care about, I would just put the segment on 100% brightness and ON, so that the master settings are always applied fully.

Don't know if this is the same issue but since upgrading to 0.111b2 none of my wled will turn on. They work fine with the wled app but turning on via HA the switch just resets to off and no lights turn on. This breaks both automation's and manual control with both single segment controllers and multi segment
Yes, this is related. Working on a solution right now.

Opened https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/36529

Addresses this, and implements the suggestion by @balloob. When a single segment is defined, a single entity in HA is created. It controls the master values in those cases and ensures the segment values match correctly. If a manual change is made outside of HA, the brightness and power state values will be correctly calculated in HA.

For multi-segment cases, a master light is created for controlling power & brightness. In those cases, the light entities that control segments, will not touch the master.
